references.text: Joseph's dreams about his brothers bowing down to him, which now begin to be fulfilled as they come to Egypt to buy grain.
Joseph's brothers betrayed him by selling him to the Ishmaelites, leading to his arrival in Egypt – the background for the reunion in this verse.
The famine that struck all lands caused people from around the world to come to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain – the background for the brothers' arrival.
Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him. He remembered the dreams he had about them – a direct continuation that expands on the recognition and harsh treatment.
Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers and explains how God's plan brought him to Egypt to preserve life – the climax of what begins in 42:7.
Stephen refers to Joseph's story in Acts, including how his brothers did not recognize him at their first visit but were recognized at the second.
Ironical role reversal: The father Jacob asked the brothers about their origin, while the son Joseph now asks the same question to test them.
Dramatic contrast between Joseph hiding himself (42:7) and Joseph revealing his identity (45:4).
Comparison of the brothers' arrival from Canaan seen through fear (42:7) and through Joseph's planned presentation to Pharaoh (46:31).
Narrative continuation: From the first meeting marked by fear (42:7) to the formal recognition of the family in Goshen (47:1).
Contrast in the search: The innocent hunt for the brothers before the betrayal (37:17) versus the strategic confrontation after Joseph gains power (42:7).
Emotional contrast: From harshness and concealment (42:7) to shocking revelation and questions about their father (45:3).
Joseph's testing strategy: From asking about their origin (42:7) to accusing them of repaying evil (44:4).
Contrast in the encounter: The dangerous journey of the brothers before the betrayal (37:13) versus the controlled confrontation later (42:7).
Turning point in status: From coming from Canaan under suspicion (42:7) to being sent back there to fetch their father (45:17).
Causality: The global famine and Joseph's preparations (Gen 41:56) are the reason why the brothers had to go to Egypt (Gen 42:7).
